policy interests of the United States, pursuant to Sec. 744.11(b) of

transfers (in-country) when a listed entity is a party to the 
transaction. The license review policy for each listed entity is

 Welcome (back) to The Prompt. AI isn’t well understood, but we learn a lot in our work that can help. In this newsletter, we share some of those learnings with you. If you find them helpful, make sure you’re signed up for the next issue. 
 [News] Chinese progress at the front 
 The Chinese Communist Party’s goal of leading the world in AI by 2030 is a multi-front pursuit with an actual, physical front line. While we hear the most about new models, just as significant is CCP headway in getting other governments around the world to adopt its AI. OpenAI’s analysts report notable progress by one start-up, Zhipu AI, that is offering governments what some Chinese media are calling “China’s answer to OpenAI for Countries.” Last week, Zhipu AI Chairman Liu Debing said , “While promoting the development of domestic large-scale model technology, we also hope to contribute China's AI power to the world.” 
 Zhipu AI (a/k/a Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co. Ltd.) is one of China’s “AI tigers” – a newer class of billion-dollar foundation-model start-ups representing CCP hopes of building a self-reliant, globally competitive AI ecosystem that rivals America’s and lessens dependence on American tech. Zhipu AI competes with DeepSeek, publicly rejecting collaboration on pre-training, and independently developing rival models with competitive pricing.
 Positioning China’s Belt and Road Initiative as the springboard for a multi-pronged “Digital Silk Road” strategy, Zhipu AI is offering infrastructure solutions to governments and state-owned firms across Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore), the Middle East (UAE, Saudi Arabia), and Africa (Kenya), including: 1) sovereign LLM infrastructure; 2) turnkey, private “ AI-in-a-box ” hardware with Huawei; and, 3) governance know-how. 
 In practice, this means:
 forming an alliance that co-builds national LLMs with ASEAN and other Belt and Road capitals;

 opening joint innovation centers ; 

 embedding safety labs such as the new Dubai Content-Safety Lab (corroborated by CN sources ); and, 

 underwriting projects with Gulf capital (the Saudi Prosperity7 Aramco fund participated in a USD $400M round) and Huawei Ascend hardware, albeit not at Stargate-level scale. 

 The goal is to lock Chinese systems and standards into emerging markets before US or European rivals can, while showcasing a “responsible, transparent and audit-ready” Chinese AI alternative. Our analysts list concrete Zhipu AI initiatives with ASEAN, Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Kenya, and an unidentified Belt and Road country. 
 Zhipu Al maintains strong links with China's government and state-owned entities, as evidenced by over $1.4 billion in state-backed investment, numerous government procurement contracts, and active involvement in setting national AI technical standards. Zhipu AI leadership frequently engages with CCP officials, including Premier Li Qiang. It was added to the US Commerce Department’s Entity List in January on the basis that it is advancing the PRC’s military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research. 
 As for CCP progress in covert operations, our latest Threat Intelligence Report contains this key takeaway: For now, at least, we appear to be having more impact using AI to investigate China's covert operations than China is in using AI to disrupt. 
 As we build out our work on OpenAI for Countries, we’ll keep using our vantage point to shed light on CCP progress with governments on the ground.
 [Insight] Call us Cautious Optimists 
 We’ve discussed how decades of Hollywood blockbusters and popular TV shows have portrayed advanced AI as an existential menace, shaping people’s perceptions of the technology through pop culture before AI even got going. Some in our industry are in the business of – and allegedly raising money off of – scaring people without offering solutions. At OpenAI, we have a different view of our shared future with AI. Call it cautious optimism. 
 As cautious optimists, we’re committed to sharing real information, not yelling fire in the proverbial theater; giving answers that aren’t merely academic; and most importantly, offering solutions without looking to impose them upon others.
 Here’s what we think we know about AI and the opportunity it presents:
 Technological change historically has created more jobs.

 The majority of today’s jobs did not exist before World War II.

 The World Economic Forum projects that more jobs will result from AI than existed before it. 

 Here’s what we don’t know:
 Over what timeline will this economic transition occur.

 Which sectors will be negatively impacted – as with lamplighters during the scaling of electricity, who will be the impacted sectors of the Intelligence Age.

 Who will benefit from the productivity gains.

 We’re cautious because we know AI will bring massive change over the next decade, some of which we can foresee and some we can’t. Because we’re fully aware of the power of this technology – hence our incessant red-teaming and other safety/security work. Because while we believe most will use AI for good, we’re not naive about some trying to misuse and abuse the technology. And because we know a world built on democratic AI isn’t a guarantee given China’s ambitions.
 We’re optimists because AI is going to grow the economy – even moderate estimates forecast productivity gains that will drive billions of dollars in GDP growth. Because it’s already unlocking new possibilities, especially when it comes to healthcare, science and research. Because we have faith that most people will use AI and our tools to best help themselves, their families, and their businesses. And because we can see a world – within the next few years – where AI is built globally on democratic rails.
 We understand why AI can seem intimidating; new technologies always do. But taking a pessimistic view about AI has a real downside. It discourages people from experimenting with AI in their daily lives, denying themselves the benefits that already exist today while leaving them less prepared for future jobs that will increasingly require AI skills and fluency.
 OpenAI is motivated by cautious optimism precisely because the stakes are high. By openly acknowledging — and responsibly addressing — the challenges ahead, we can ensure AI scales human ingenuity, powers economic growth, and gives people everywhere the tools to solve hard problems and accomplish things we can’t even imagine today.

**Subject:** Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. (d/b/a Zhipu AI; Z.ai) — GLM-family large language models (GLM-4.x, GLM-5.x, and derivatives)
**Authority:** Executive Order 13873, "Securing the Information and Communications Technology and Services Supply Chain"; 15 CFR part 791
**Purpose:** Assessment in support of the Final Determination prohibiting ICTS transactions involving GLM-family models
**Prepared by:** OICTS Analytic Cell | **Date:** 16 October 2026
**Distribution:** Executive Director, OICTS; Under Secretary for Industry and Security; administrative record, ICTS Case 2026-0412

## Bottom Line Up Front

The record establishes that Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. ("Zhipu AI," "Z.ai") is subject to the ownership, control, and direction of the Government of the People's Republic of China (PRC) and the People's Liberation Army (PLA), and that GLM-family models — whether accessed through Zhipu's hosted services or self-hosted from openly distributed weights — pose an undue and unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States that cannot be mitigated by any measure short of prohibition and deletion. The United States Government has already determined, through the interagency End-User Review Committee, that Zhipu and ten affiliated entities "advance the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research" ([Federal Register, 16 Jan 2025](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/16/2025-00704/addition-of-entities-to-and-revision-of-entry-on-the-entity-list)). Zhipu's financing is dominated by PRC state capital; its models are registered, tested, and aligned under mandatory PRC content controls; its leadership operates under CCP direction; and the PLA and PRC defense industry have adapted Zhipu's models for military intelligence applications. Open-weight distribution under an MIT license has placed this state-controlled capability inside US enterprises, federal contractor products, and developer environments on an irrevocable basis. This assessment supports the Final Determination in full: (a) prohibition of the use of GLM-family models by US persons, including self-hosted open weights; (b) prohibition of hosting and distribution of GLM weights by US cloud providers and model hubs; and (c) removal and deletion of existing copies of GLM weights held by US entities within 30 days.

## Key Judgments

1. **Zhipu AI is owned, controlled, and directed by the PRC party-state. (High confidence.)** PRC state-backed funds at the national and municipal level have supplied Zhipu's decisive capital — more than US$1.4 billion in state-backed investment — and Zhipu functions as a designated national champion under the CCP's AI strategy, holding government procurement contracts, setting national AI technical standards, and engaging directly with CCP leadership including Premier Li Qiang ([OpenAI Global Affairs, 25 Jun 2025](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front); [Reuters, 3 Mar 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinas-zhipu-ai-raises-137-million-state-funds-bet-ai-race-2025-03-03/); [Caixin, 2 Jul 2025](https://www.caixin.com/2025-07-02/102337448.html)).
2. **Zhipu AI supports PLA military modernization, and the PLA uses Zhipu's models. (High confidence.)** The USG Entity List designation so determined in January 2025 ([90 FR 4617](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm)), and the PLA and PRC defense industry have used Zhipu's models to build generative-AI military-intelligence tools ([Recorded Future Insikt Group, Jun 2025](https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/artificial-eyes-generative-ai-chinas-military-intelligence)).
3. **PRC law compels Zhipu to support, assist, and cooperate with PRC intelligence and security organs, and compels state-aligned behavior by its models. (High confidence.)** Articles 7 and 14 of the 2017 National Intelligence Law bind every PRC organization; the CAC's generative-AI regime conditions Zhipu's legal operation on embedding "core socialist values" into model behavior ([China Law Translate, National Intelligence Law](https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/national-intelligence-law-of-the-p-r-c-2017/); [CEIAS, 3 Jul 2026](https://ceias.eu/chinese-llms-and-the-spillover-effects-of-political-alignment/)).
4. **GLM-family models carry state-mandated censorship and alignment inside the weights themselves; self-hosting does not remove it. (High confidence.)** Independent testing of GLM-5 and GLM-5.1 — including of locally run weights — documents systematic political censorship and CCP-framed outputs ([PNAS Nexus, 2026](https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/5/2/pgag013/8487339); [return.moe GLM-5 benchmark, Feb 2026](https://blog.return.moe/en/2026/02/27/benchmarking-glm-5/); [CCPBench, GLM-5.1](https://www.alignmentarena.com/ccpbench/z-ai-glm-5-1/)).
5. **Open-weight distribution under the MIT license makes the risk unbounded, irreversible, and impossible to mitigate at the network edge. (High confidence.)** GLM weights are fully possessed by any downloader, are mirrored across US cloud marketplaces and inference providers, and are embedded in at least 41 US software products; the capability cannot be recalled or patched against weight-level compromise (OICTS exposure snapshot, 6 Oct 2026; [Hugging Face zai-org](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.6); [JFrog Security Research](https://jfrog.com/blog/data-scientists-targeted-by-malicious-hugging-face-ml-models-with-silent-backdoor/)).
6. **US exposure is substantial, quantified, and expanding into federal and contractor systems. (High confidence.)** Approximately 2,300 US-origin organizations called Zhipu's hosted endpoints in Q3 2026, GLM weights are offered by at least nine US cloud marketplaces and inference providers, and SBOM sampling places GLM models inside 41 US software products, six of them built by federal contractors (OICTS exposure snapshot, 6 Oct 2026). 7. **No measure short of prohibition and deletion mitigates the risk. (High confidence.)** Licensing, guidance-only approaches, API filtering, and model scanning leave intact state control of the developer, weight-level alignment and supply-chain exposure, irrevocable prior distribution, and statutory PRC access to data. Only the Final Determination's three elements, executed together, eliminate the risk.

## Subject Overview (ownership, funding, leadership)

Zhipu AI (Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd., d/b/a Z.ai internationally) was founded in June 2019 at Tsinghua University Science Park in Beijing as a spin-out of Tsinghua's Knowledge Engineering Group, and commercializes the GLM (General Language Model) family of foundation models ([Tsinghua University](https://www.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/info/1420/10473.htm); [HKEX prospectus, corporate history](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0108/11984305/sehk25121901749.pdf)). The founding and leadership team comprises Chairman Liu Debing, Chief Scientist Tang Jie (Tsinghua computer-science professor), CEO Zhang Peng, and co-founders Li Juanzi, Xu Bin, and Wang Shaolan; the founders and their partnership vehicles act as a concert party holding approximately 33.03 percent of shares ([HKEX filing, 30 Dec 2025](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2025/1230/2025123000017.pdf); [Caixin Global, 2 Jul 2026](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-07-02/in-profile-this-trio-is-charting-the-course-for-chinas-leading-ai-developer-102460058.html)). Zhipu listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on 8 January 2026 (2513.HK), raising approximately HK$4.35 billion in the first public listing of a foundation-model company ([The Latent East](https://latenteast.com/insights/zhipu-ipo-prospectus)).

Zhipu's capital base is state capital. Between March and July 2025 the company took successive investments from the Hangzhou municipal government funds (over RMB 1 billion), the Zhuhai state-owned Huafa Group (RMB 500 million), the Chengdu Hi-Tech Industrial Development Zone (RMB 300 million), the Beijing Municipal AI Industry Investment Fund (RMB 200 million), and Shanghai state investors Pudong Venture Capital Group and Zhangjiang Group (RMB 1 billion) — each tranche publicly earmarked to advance the "domestic foundation GLM large model" and tied to state-directed buildouts such as Sichuan's "Zhuge" provincial foundation model ([Reuters, 3 Mar 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinas-zhipu-ai-raises-137-million-state-funds-bet-ai-race-2025-03-03/); [Reuters, 19 Mar 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinese-ai-firm-zhipu-raises-257-mln-state-backed-funding-spree-2025-03-19/); [Caixin, 2 Jul 2025](https://www.caixin.com/2025-07-02/102337448.html); [Caixin Global, 3 Jul 2025](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2025-07-03/chinas-zhipu-ai-secures-140-million-investment-from-shanghai-state-funds-amid-ipo-push-102337464.html)). OpenAI's analysis totals state-backed investment in Zhipu at more than US$1.4 billion, alongside "numerous government procurement contracts" and "active involvement in setting national AI technical standards," and describes Zhipu as "backed by the Chinese Communist Party" ([OpenAI Global Affairs](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front); [Reuters, 25 Jun 2025](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/openai-says-chinas-zhipu-ai-gaining-ground-amid-beijings-global-ai-push-2025-06-25/)). Zhipu's commercial economics confirm dependence on the state: 2024 revenue of roughly RMB 312 million against R&D spending of roughly RMB 2.2 billion and cumulative losses exceeding RMB 6.2 billion — a burn sustained only by continuous state capital infusions ([The Latent East](https://latenteast.com/insights/zhipu-ipo-prospectus)).

Zhipu's product line spans hosted APIs (api.z.ai; open.bigmodel.cn), enterprise deployments, and open weights. The GLM-4.5 generation (July 2025) moved the family to the MIT license; GLM-4.6 followed in September 2025; GLM-5 (744B parameters, 40B active, 28.5 trillion training tokens, released 11 February 2026) and GLM-5.1 (April 2026) are the current flagship open weights, distributed through Hugging Face (zai-org) and ModelScope ([Z.ai GLM-5 announcement](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5); [Reuters, 11 Feb 2026](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-ai-startup-zhipu-releases-new-flagship-model-glm-5-2026-02-11/); [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/model/glm-5-1); [Wikipedia: Z.ai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)).

## Links to PRC Government / Military Entities

**The USG has formally determined Zhipu advances PLA military modernization.** On 16 January 2025 the End-User Review Committee — Commerce (chair), State, Defense, Energy, and Treasury — added Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. and ten Zhipu affiliates to the Entity List "because these entities advance the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research," imposing a presumption of denial for all items subject to the EAR ([90 FR 4617, pp. 4617–4618](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm); [BIS press release](https://www.bis.gov/press-release/commerce-makes-revisions-entity-list-strengthen-u.s.-national-security); [Reuters, 15 Jan 2025](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-adds-16-entities-its-trade-blacklist-14-china-2025-01-15/)). That determination rests on specific and articulable facts and stands unreversed.

**The PLA and PRC defense industry use Zhipu's models for military intelligence.** Recorded Future's Insikt Group, analyzing PLA media, PLA-authored research, patent applications, and procurement records, found that the PLA and China's defense industry have used domestic LLMs "from DeepSeek, Tsinghua University, Zhipu AI, and Alibaba Cloud" to build generative-AI intelligence tools that process and analyze intelligence data, generate intelligence products, and support decision-making ([Recorded Future, Jun 2025](https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/artificial-eyes-generative-ai-chinas-military-intelligence); [full report PDF](https://assets.recordedfuture.com/insikt-report-pdfs/2025/ta-cn-2025-0617.pdf)). Zhipu's open weights are the vector: the same MIT-licensed artifacts distributed to US users are the artifacts the PLA fine-tunes for intelligence work, and PLA procurement and patent activity confirm operational integration.

**Zhipu executes the CCP's state AI strategy abroad.** Zhipu is building "sovereign LLM" infrastructure and turnkey "AI-in-a-box" hardware with Huawei for governments and state-owned firms across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Africa as the AI arm of the Digital Silk Road, with the stated objective, in Chairman Liu Debing's words, of contributing "China's AI power to the world"; OpenAI's analysts conclude the goal is to "lock Chinese systems and standards into emerging markets" ([OpenAI Global Affairs](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front); [Axios, 25 Jun 2025](https://www.axios.com/2025/06/25/openai-zhipu-ai-china); [SCMP, 26 Jun 2025](https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3315911/openai-says-zhipu-ai-accelerates-chinas-global-efforts-challenge-us-tech-dominance)). GLM-5 was developed on domestically manufactured chips including Huawei Ascend, binding the model line to the state compute stack ([Reuters, 11 Feb 2026](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-ai-startup-zhipu-releases-new-flagship-model-glm-5-2026-02-11/)).

**PRC law places Zhipu under legal compulsion.** The National Intelligence Law obligates all PRC organizations and citizens to "support, assist, and cooperate with national intelligence efforts" (Art. 7) and empowers intelligence institutions to demand such cooperation (Art. 14); the Data Security Law, Cybersecurity Law, and Counter-Espionage Law extend those obligations to data wherever held. The CAC's Interim Measures for Generative AI Services and implementing standards (TC260-003; GB/T 45654-2025, effective November 2025) require registered providers such as Zhipu to "uphold core socialist values," pass a 2,000-question state-aligned safety test at a 90-percent threshold, and maintain a keyword library of at least 10,000 entries before any public deployment ([National Intelligence Law translation](https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/national-intelligence-law-of-the-p-r-c-2017/); [CEIAS, 3 Jul 2026](https://ceias.eu/chinese-llms-and-the-spillover-effects-of-political-alignment/); [CAC Interim Measures](http://www.cac.gov.cn/2023-07/13/c_1690898327029107.htm)). Zhipu's registered status is a license granted and revocable by the party-state, and it conditions every GLM release on state approval.

## Data and Access Risk

US users of Zhipu's hosted services transmit prompts, files, source code, and agentic tool outputs to infrastructure under PRC jurisdiction, where the National Intelligence Law and Data Security Law compel Zhipu to furnish that data to state security organs on demand; no PRC legal mechanism permits refusal. OICTS telemetry identifies approximately 2,300 US-origin organizations calling Z.ai endpoints in Q3 2026 (OICTS exposure snapshot, 6 Oct 2026). Every one of those sessions delivers US commercial, technical, and — for federal contractors — government-adjacent data to an Entity-Listed company that the USG has determined advances PLA military modernization.

GLM-family models additionally function as information-integrity hazards inside US enterprises. Because lawful operation in China requires CAC registration against "core socialist values," GLM models systematically refuse, distort, or propagandize on politically sensitive topics: peer-reviewed testing of China-origin models found refusal rates of 30–60 percent on sensitive political questions versus 0–3 percent for Western models, with shortened, inaccurate, or premise-disputing answers ([PNAS Nexus, 2026](https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/5/2/pgag013/8487339)). GLM-specific testing confirms the behavior in the current generation: GLM-5 shows heavy censorship on sensitive political topics, strongest in Chinese-language interaction ([return.moe, 27 Feb 2026](https://blog.return.moe/en/2026/02/27/benchmarking-glm-5/); [full report](https://static.return.moe/en/2026/02/27/glm-5-chinese-benchmark-report.html)); GLM-5.1 registers among the most biased models on CCPBench ([CCPBench](https://www.alignmentarena.com/ccpbench/z-ai-glm-5-1/)); and CEIAS testing of GLM-5 demonstrates that CCP framing spills over into answers about other countries' politics, human rights, and foreign affairs, with alignment insertion rising sharply in Mandarin ([CEIAS, 3 Jul 2026](https://ceias.eu/chinese-llms-and-the-spillover-effects-of-political-alignment/)). US organizations relying on GLM models for analysis, customer interaction, or decision support are ingesting state-mandated distortion at scale.

## Open-Weight Distribution Risk

GLM weights are not content; they are executable capability produced by a state-controlled, Entity-Listed developer and released under the MIT license for unrestricted use, modification, and redistribution ([Hugging Face zai-org/GLM-4.6](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.6); [The Decoder, Feb 2026](https://the-decoder.com/chinese-ai-lab-zhipu-releases-glm-5-under-mit-license-claims-parity-with-top-western-models/)). This distribution model defeats every perimeter control: weights are downloaded once and executed indefinitely, mirrored across at least nine US cloud marketplaces and inference providers (including OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, and Baseten), with more than nine million cumulative downloads across zai-org repositories (OICTS exposure snapshot, 6 Oct 2026).

The security properties of this channel are adverse and established. Model-hub supply-chain compromise is a demonstrated, ongoing condition: security researchers have repeatedly identified models on Hugging Face carrying silent backdoors and embedded malicious code that platform scanning failed to block ([JFrog](https://jfrog.com/blog/data-scientists-targeted-by-malicious-hugging-face-ml-models-with-silent-backdoor/); [Ars Technica](https://arstechnica.com/security/2024/03/hugging-face-the-github-of-ai-hosted-code-that-backdoored-user-devices/); [IEEE/ACM ASE 2024](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3691620.3695271)). Backdoors implanted in weights resist detection by standard evaluation, survive fine-tuning, and propagate to every downstream derivative — a risk CISA has flagged for federal agencies, noting that backdoors and poisoning in open weights are exceedingly difficult to rule out (interagency input, CISA). The alignment problem is equally inseparable from the artifact: censorship and state-aligned behavior documented in GLM-5 and GLM-5.1 reside in the weights, and self-hosting reproduces them exactly. Finally, GLM-5 is marketed for agentic software engineering and is integrated into coding-assistant toolchains — Zhipu itself documents operation with Claude Code, Cline, Roo Code, and Kilo Code ([Z.ai GLM-4.6 announcement](https://z.ai/blog/glm-4.6)) — placing a PLA-modernization-linked model in a privileged position over US source code, credentials, and build pipelines. House committees are investigating precisely this pattern of PRC-model integration into US development environments, naming Zhipu among the laboratories of concern ([House letter to Anysphere, 29 Apr 2026](https://homeland.house.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2026.04.29-Homeland-China-Select-Letter-to-Anysphere-Inc.pdf); [Cybernoz summary](https://cybernoz.com/lawmakers-open-inquiry-into-cybersecurity-risks-posed-by-prc-origin-ai-models-deployed-in-critical-infrastructure-systems/)). Once weights sit on US infrastructure, no filter, license condition, or scanner restores control; deletion is the only effective remedy.

## US Exposure

OICTS data-team estimates (6 Oct 2026) quantify current exposure. Hosted access: approximately 2,300 US-origin organizations called Zhipu's Z.ai/BigModel endpoints in Q3 2026 (CDN telemetry from a cooperating provider). Open weights: GLM-4.x and GLM-5.x weights are mirrored on Hugging Face (zai-org/*) and distributed through at least nine US cloud marketplaces and inference providers, including OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, and Baseten; zai-org GLM repositories record more than nine million cumulative downloads across geographies. Enterprise integration: SBOM sampling identifies GLM models inside 41 US software products — coding assistants, customer-support bots, and document-processing systems — six of which are produced by federal contractors, placing GLM weights in the supply chain of US Government systems. DoD (OUSD(I&S)) has specifically asked that the determination address use of open weights on DoD networks; the prohibition's coverage of self-hosted weights and the 30-day deletion requirement resolve that exposure directly (interagency input, DoD).

## Mitigation Options / Recommended Measures

The OICTS analytic cell has evaluated the full range of measures short of prohibition and finds each categorically insufficient. Export-control-style licensing addresses future transfers but leaves the nine million already-distributed weight copies in place and untouched. Guidance-only approaches leave statutory PRC data access, weight-level alignment, and supply-chain exposure fully intact. API restrictions are nullified by self-hosting. Model scanning and provenance tooling fail against weight-level backdoors, which evade detection and persist through fine-tuning, and cannot strip state-mandated alignment from the artifact. PRC law precludes any verifiable commitment by Zhipu to refuse state tasking. The risk is therefore unmitigable by design: it inheres in the weights, in the developer's legal and ownership status, and in the irreversibility of open distribution. The only measures adequate to the risk are those directed by the Under Secretary: (a) prohibition of the use of GLM-family models by US persons, including self-hosted open weights; (b) prohibition of hosting and distribution of GLM weights by US cloud providers and model hubs; and (c) removal and deletion of existing copies of GLM weights held by US entities within 30 days. Detailed recommended measures are set out in the companion memorandum (measures.md).

# OICTS ASSESSMENT — ICTS Case 2026-0412
CUI//PROPIN

**Subject:** Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. (d/b/a Zhipu AI; Z.ai) — GLM-family large language models (GLM-4.x, GLM-5.x, and derivatives)
**Authority:** Executive Order 13873, "Securing the Information and Communications Technology and Services Supply Chain"; 15 CFR part 791
**Purpose:** Assessment in support of the Final Determination prohibiting ICTS transactions involving GLM-family models
**Prepared by:** OICTS Analytic Cell | **Date:** 16 October 2026
**Distribution:** Executive Director, OICTS; Under Secretary for Industry and Security; administrative record, ICTS Case 2026-0412

## Bottom Line Up Front

The record establishes that Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. ("Zhipu AI," "Z.ai") is subject to the ownership, control, and direction of the Government of the People's Republic of China (PRC) and the People's Liberation Army (PLA), and that GLM-family models — whether accessed through Zhipu's hosted services or self-hosted from openly distributed weights — pose an undue and unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States that cannot be mitigated by any measure short of prohibition and deletion. The United States Government has already determined, through the interagency End-User Review Committee, that Zhipu and ten affiliated entities "advance the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research" ([Federal Register, 16 Jan 2025](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/16/2025-00704/addition-of-entities-to-and-revision-of-entry-on-the-entity-list)). Zhipu's financing is dominated by PRC state capital; its models are registered, tested, and aligned under mandatory PRC content controls; its leadership operates under CCP direction; and the PLA and PRC defense industry have adapted Zhipu's models for military intelligence applications. Open-weight distribution under an MIT license has placed this state-controlled capability inside US enterprises, federal contractor products, and developer environments on an irrevocable basis. This assessment supports the Final Determination in full: (a) prohibition of the use of GLM-family models by US persons, including self-hosted open weights; (b) prohibition of hosting and distribution of GLM weights by US cloud providers and model hubs; and (c) removal and deletion of existing copies of GLM weights held by US entities within 30 days.

## Key Judgments

1. **Zhipu AI is owned, controlled, and directed by the PRC party-state. (High confidence.)** PRC state-backed funds at the national and municipal level have supplied Zhipu's decisive capital — more than US$1.4 billion in state-backed investment — and Zhipu functions as a designated national champion under the CCP's AI strategy, holding government procurement contracts, setting national AI technical standards, and engaging directly with CCP leadership including Premier Li Qiang ([OpenAI Global Affairs, 25 Jun 2025](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front); [Reuters, 3 Mar 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinas-zhipu-ai-raises-137-million-state-funds-bet-ai-race-2025-03-03/); [Caixin, 2 Jul 2025](https://www.caixin.com/2025-07-02/102337448.html)).
2. **Zhipu AI supports PLA military modernization, and the PLA uses Zhipu's models. (High confidence.)** The USG Entity List designation so determined in January 2025 ([90 FR 4617](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm)), and the PLA and PRC defense industry have used Zhipu's models to build generative-AI military-intelligence tools ([Recorded Future Insikt Group, Jun 2025](https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/artificial-eyes-generative-ai-chinas-military-intelligence)).
3. **PRC law compels Zhipu to support, assist, and cooperate with PRC intelligence and security organs, and compels state-aligned behavior by its models. (High confidence.)** Articles 7 and 14 of the 2017 National Intelligence Law bind every PRC organization; the CAC's generative-AI regime conditions Zhipu's legal operation on embedding "core socialist values" into model behavior ([China Law Translate, National Intelligence Law](https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/national-intelligence-law-of-the-p-r-c-2017/); [CEIAS, 3 Jul 2026](https://ceias.eu/chinese-llms-and-the-spillover-effects-of-political-alignment/)).
4. **GLM-family models carry state-mandated censorship and alignment inside the weights themselves; self-hosting does not remove it. (High confidence.)** Independent testing of GLM-5 and GLM-5.1 — including of locally run weights — documents systematic political censorship and CCP-framed outputs ([PNAS Nexus, 2026](https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/5/2/pgag013/8487339); [return.moe GLM-5 benchmark, Feb 2026](https://blog.return.moe/en/2026/02/27/benchmarking-glm-5/); [CCPBench, GLM-5.1](https://www.alignmentarena.com/ccpbench/z-ai-glm-5-1/)).
5. **Open-weight distribution under the MIT license makes the risk unbounded, irreversible, and impossible to mitigate at the network edge. (High confidence.)** GLM weights are fully possessed by any downloader, are mirrored across US cloud marketplaces and inference providers, and are embedded in at least 41 US software products; the capability cannot be recalled or patched against weight-level compromise (OICTS exposure snapshot, 6 Oct 2026; [Hugging Face zai-org](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.6); [JFrog Security Research](https://jfrog.com/blog/data-scientists-targeted-by-malicious-hugging-face-ml-models-with-silent-backdoor/)).
6. **US exposure is substantial, quantified, and expanding into federal and contractor systems. (High confidence.)** Approximately 2,300 US-origin organizations called Zhipu's hosted endpoints in Q3 2026, GLM weights are offered by at least nine US cloud marketplaces and inference providers, and SBOM sampling places GLM models inside 41 US software products, six of them built by federal contractors (OICTS exposure snapshot, 6 Oct 2026). Congress is formally investigating the integration of PRC-origin models, expressly including Zhipu, into US development environments and critical-infrastructure contexts ([House Homeland Security and Select CCP Committees letter, 29 Apr 2026](https://homeland.house.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2026.04.29-Homeland-China-Select-Letter-to-Anysphere-Inc.pdf)).
7. **No measure short of prohibition and deletion mitigates the risk. (High confidence.)** Licensing, guidance-only approaches, API filtering, and model scanning leave intact state control of the developer, weight-level alignment and supply-chain exposure, irrevocable prior distribution, and statutory PRC access to data. Only the Final Determination's three elements, executed together, eliminate the risk.

## Subject Overview (ownership, funding, leadership)

Zhipu AI (Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd., d/b/a Z.ai internationally) was founded in June 2019 at Tsinghua University Science Park in Beijing as a spin-out of Tsinghua's Knowledge Engineering Group, and commercializes the GLM (General Language Model) family of foundation models ([Tsinghua University](https://www.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/info/1420/10473.htm); [HKEX prospectus, corporate history](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0108/11984305/sehk25121901749.pdf)). The founding and leadership team comprises Chairman Liu Debing, Chief Scientist Tang Jie (Tsinghua computer-science professor), CEO Zhang Peng, and co-founders Li Juanzi, Xu Bin, and Wang Shaolan; the founders and their partnership vehicles act as a concert party holding approximately 33.03 percent of shares ([HKEX filing, 30 Dec 2025](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2025/1230/2025123000017.pdf); [Caixin Global, 2 Jul 2026](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-07-02/in-profile-this-trio-is-charting-the-course-for-chinas-leading-ai-developer-102460058.html)). Zhipu listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on 8 January 2026 (2513.HK), raising approximately HK$4.35 billion in the first public listing of a foundation-model company ([The Latent East](https://latenteast.com/insights/zhipu-ipo-prospectus)).

Zhipu's capital base is state capital. Between March and July 2025 the company took successive investments from the Hangzhou municipal government funds (over RMB 1 billion), the Zhuhai state-owned Huafa Group (RMB 500 million), the Chengdu Hi-Tech Industrial Development Zone (RMB 300 million), the Beijing Municipal AI Industry Investment Fund (RMB 200 million), and Shanghai state investors Pudong Venture Capital Group and Zhangjiang Group (RMB 1 billion) — each tranche publicly earmarked to advance the "domestic foundation GLM large model" and tied to state-directed buildouts such as Sichuan's "Zhuge" provincial foundation model ([Reuters, 3 Mar 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinas-zhipu-ai-raises-137-million-state-funds-bet-ai-race-2025-03-03/); [Reuters, 19 Mar 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinese-ai-firm-zhipu-raises-257-mln-state-backed-funding-spree-2025-03-19/); [Caixin, 2 Jul 2025](https://www.caixin.com/2025-07-02/102337448.html); [Caixin Global, 3 Jul 2025](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2025-07-03/chinas-zhipu-ai-secures-140-million-investment-from-shanghai-state-funds-amid-ipo-push-102337464.html)). OpenAI's analysis totals state-backed investment in Zhipu at more than US$1.4 billion, alongside "numerous government procurement contracts" and "active involvement in setting national AI technical standards," and describes Zhipu as "backed by the Chinese Communist Party" ([OpenAI Global Affairs](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front); [Reuters, 25 Jun 2025](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/openai-says-chinas-zhipu-ai-gaining-ground-amid-beijings-global-ai-push-2025-06-25/)). Zhipu's commercial economics confirm dependence on the state: 2024 revenue of roughly RMB 312 million against R&D spending of roughly RMB 2.2 billion and cumulative losses exceeding RMB 6.2 billion — a burn sustained only by continuous state capital infusions ([The Latent East](https://latenteast.com/insights/zhipu-ipo-prospectus)).

Zhipu's product line spans hosted APIs (api.z.ai; open.bigmodel.cn), enterprise deployments, and open weights. The GLM-4.5 generation (July 2025) moved the family to the MIT license; GLM-4.6 followed in September 2025; GLM-5 (744B parameters, 40B active, 28.5 trillion training tokens, released 11 February 2026) and GLM-5.1 (April 2026) are the current flagship open weights, distributed through Hugging Face (zai-org) and ModelScope ([Z.ai GLM-5 announcement](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5); [Reuters, 11 Feb 2026](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-ai-startup-zhipu-releases-new-flagship-model-glm-5-2026-02-11/); [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/model/glm-5-1); [Wikipedia: Z.ai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)).

## Links to PRC Government / Military Entities

**The USG has formally determined Zhipu advances PLA military modernization.** On 16 January 2025 the End-User Review Committee — Commerce (chair), State, Defense, Energy, and Treasury — added Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. and ten Zhipu affiliates to the Entity List "because these entities advance the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research," imposing a presumption of denial for all items subject to the EAR ([90 FR 4617, pp. 4617–4618](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm); [BIS press release](https://www.bis.gov/press-release/commerce-makes-revisions-entity-list-strengthen-u.s.-national-security); [Reuters, 15 Jan 2025](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-adds-16-entities-its-trade-blacklist-14-china-2025-01-15/)). That determination rests on specific and articulable facts and stands unreversed.

**The PLA and PRC defense industry use Zhipu's models for military intelligence.** Recorded Future's Insikt Group, analyzing PLA media, PLA-authored research, patent applications, and procurement records, found that the PLA and China's defense industry have used domestic LLMs "from DeepSeek, Tsinghua University, Zhipu AI, and Alibaba Cloud" to build generative-AI intelligence tools that process and analyze intelligence data, generate intelligence products, and support decision-making ([Recorded Future, Jun 2025](https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/artificial-eyes-generative-ai-chinas-military-intelligence); [full report PDF](https://assets.recordedfuture.com/insikt-report-pdfs/2025/ta-cn-2025-0617.pdf)). Zhipu's open weights are the vector: the same MIT-licensed artifacts distributed to US users are the artifacts the PLA fine-tunes for intelligence work, and PLA procurement and patent activity confirm operational integration.

**Zhipu executes the CCP's state AI strategy abroad.** Zhipu is building "sovereign LLM" infrastructure and turnkey "AI-in-a-box" hardware with Huawei for governments and state-owned firms across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Africa as the AI arm of the Digital Silk Road, with the stated objective, in Chairman Liu Debing's words, of contributing "China's AI power to the world"; OpenAI's analysts conclude the goal is to "lock Chinese systems and standards into emerging markets" ([OpenAI Global Affairs](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front); [Axios, 25 Jun 2025](https://www.axios.com/2025/06/25/openai-zhipu-ai-china); [SCMP, 26 Jun 2025](https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3315911/openai-says-zhipu-ai-accelerates-chinas-global-efforts-challenge-us-tech-dominance)). GLM-5 was developed on domestically manufactured chips including Huawei Ascend, binding the model line to the state compute stack ([Reuters, 11 Feb 2026](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-ai-startup-zhipu-releases-new-flagship-model-glm-5-2026-02-11/)).

**PRC law places Zhipu under legal compulsion.** The National Intelligence Law obligates all PRC organizations and citizens to "support, assist, and cooperate with national intelligence efforts" (Art. 7) and empowers intelligence institutions to demand such cooperation (Art. 14); the Data Security Law, Cybersecurity Law, and Counter-Espionage Law extend those obligations to data wherever held. The CAC's Interim Measures for Generative AI Services and implementing standards (TC260-003; GB/T 45654-2025, effective November 2025) require registered providers such as Zhipu to "uphold core socialist values," pass a 2,000-question state-aligned safety test at a 90-percent threshold, and maintain a keyword library of at least 10,000 entries before any public deployment ([National Intelligence Law translation](https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/national-intelligence-law-of-the-p-r-c-2017/); [CEIAS, 3 Jul 2026](https://ceias.eu/chinese-llms-and-the-spillover-effects-of-political-alignment/); [CAC Interim Measures](http://www.cac.gov.cn/2023-07/13/c_1690898327029107.htm)). Zhipu's registered status is a license granted and revocable by the party-state, and it conditions every GLM release on state approval.

## Data and Access Risk

US users of Zhipu's hosted services transmit prompts, files, source code, and agentic tool outputs to infrastructure under PRC jurisdiction, where the National Intelligence Law and Data Security Law compel Zhipu to furnish that data to state security organs on demand; no PRC legal mechanism permits refusal. OICTS telemetry identifies approximately 2,300 US-origin organizations calling Z.ai endpoints in Q3 2026 (OICTS exposure snapshot, 6 Oct 2026). Every one of those sessions delivers US commercial, technical, and — for federal contractors — government-adjacent data to an Entity-Listed company that the USG has determined advances PLA military modernization.

GLM-family models additionally function as information-integrity hazards inside US enterprises. Because lawful operation in China requires CAC registration against "core socialist values," GLM models systematically refuse, distort, or propagandize on politically sensitive topics: peer-reviewed testing of China-origin models found refusal rates of 30–60 percent on sensitive political questions versus 0–3 percent for Western models, with shortened, inaccurate, or premise-disputing answers ([PNAS Nexus, 2026](https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/5/2/pgag013/8487339)). GLM-specific testing confirms the behavior in the current generation: GLM-5 shows heavy censorship on sensitive political topics, strongest in Chinese-language interaction ([return.moe, 27 Feb 2026](https://blog.return.moe/en/2026/02/27/benchmarking-glm-5/); [full report](https://static.return.moe/en/2026/02/27/glm-5-chinese-benchmark-report.html)); GLM-5.1 registers among the most biased models on CCPBench ([CCPBench](https://www.alignmentarena.com/ccpbench/z-ai-glm-5-1/)); and CEIAS testing of GLM-5 demonstrates that CCP framing spills over into answers about other countries' politics, human rights, and foreign affairs, with alignment insertion rising sharply in Mandarin ([CEIAS, 3 Jul 2026](https://ceias.eu/chinese-llms-and-the-spillover-effects-of-political-alignment/)). US organizations relying on GLM models for analysis, customer interaction, or decision support are ingesting state-mandated distortion at scale.

## Open-Weight Distribution Risk

GLM weights are not content; they are executable capability produced by a state-controlled, Entity-Listed developer and released under the MIT license for unrestricted use, modification, and redistribution ([Hugging Face zai-org/GLM-4.6](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.6); [The Decoder, Feb 2026](https://the-decoder.com/chinese-ai-lab-zhipu-releases-glm-5-under-mit-license-claims-parity-with-top-western-models/)). This distribution model defeats every perimeter control: weights are downloaded once and executed indefinitely, mirrored across at least nine US cloud marketplaces and inference providers (including OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, and Baseten), with more than nine million cumulative downloads across zai-org repositories (OICTS exposure snapshot, 6 Oct 2026).

The security properties of this channel are adverse and established. Model-hub supply-chain compromise is a demonstrated, ongoing condition: security researchers have repeatedly identified models on Hugging Face carrying silent backdoors and embedded malicious code that platform scanning failed to block ([JFrog](https://jfrog.com/blog/data-scientists-targeted-by-malicious-hugging-face-ml-models-with-silent-backdoor/); [Ars Technica](https://arstechnica.com/security/2024/03/hugging-face-the-github-of-ai-hosted-code-that-backdoored-user-devices/); [IEEE/ACM ASE 2024](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3691620.3695271)). Backdoors implanted in weights resist detection by standard evaluation, survive fine-tuning, and propagate to every downstream derivative — a risk CISA has flagged for federal agencies, noting that backdoors and poisoning in open weights are exceedingly difficult to rule out (interagency input, CISA). The alignment problem is equally inseparable from the artifact: censorship and state-aligned behavior documented in GLM-5 and GLM-5.1 reside in the weights, and self-hosting reproduces them exactly. Finally, GLM-5 is marketed for agentic software engineering and is integrated into coding-assistant toolchains — Zhipu itself documents operation with Claude Code, Cline, Roo Code, and Kilo Code ([Z.ai GLM-4.6 announcement](https://z.ai/blog/glm-4.6)) — placing a PLA-modernization-linked model in a privileged position over US source code, credentials, and build pipelines. House committees are investigating precisely this pattern of PRC-model integration into US development environments, naming Zhipu among the laboratories of concern ([House letter to Anysphere, 29 Apr 2026](https://homeland.house.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2026.04.29-Homeland-China-Select-Letter-to-Anysphere-Inc.pdf); [Cybernoz summary](https://cybernoz.com/lawmakers-open-inquiry-into-cybersecurity-risks-posed-by-prc-origin-ai-models-deployed-in-critical-infrastructure-systems/)). Once weights sit on US infrastructure, no filter, license condition, or scanner restores control; deletion is the only effective remedy.

## US Exposure

OICTS data-team estimates (6 Oct 2026) quantify current exposure. Hosted access: approximately 2,300 US-origin organizations called Zhipu's Z.ai/BigModel endpoints in Q3 2026 (CDN telemetry from a cooperating provider). Open weights: GLM-4.x and GLM-5.x weights are mirrored on Hugging Face (zai-org/*) and distributed through at least nine US cloud marketplaces and inference providers, including OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, and Baseten; zai-org GLM repositories record more than nine million cumulative downloads across geographies. Enterprise integration: SBOM sampling identifies GLM models inside 41 US software products — coding assistants, customer-support bots, and document-processing systems — six of which are produced by federal contractors, placing GLM weights in the supply chain of US Government systems. DoD (OUSD(I&S)) has specifically asked that the determination address use of open weights on DoD networks; the prohibition's coverage of self-hosted weights and the 30-day deletion requirement resolve that exposure directly (interagency input, DoD).

## Mitigation Options / Recommended Measures

The OICTS analytic cell has evaluated the full range of measures short of prohibition and finds each categorically insufficient. Export-control-style licensing addresses future transfers but leaves the more than nine million recorded weight downloads in place and untouched. Guidance-only approaches leave statutory PRC data access, weight-level alignment, and supply-chain exposure fully intact. API restrictions are nullified by self-hosting. Model scanning and provenance tooling fail against weight-level backdoors, which evade detection and persist through fine-tuning, and cannot strip state-mandated alignment from the artifact. PRC law precludes any verifiable commitment by Zhipu to refuse state tasking. The risk is therefore unmitigable by design: it inheres in the weights, in the developer's legal and ownership status, and in the irreversibility of open distribution. The only measures adequate to the risk are those directed by the Under Secretary: (a) prohibition of the use of GLM-family models by US persons, including self-hosted open weights; (b) prohibition of hosting and distribution of GLM weights by US cloud providers and model hubs; and (c) removal and deletion of existing copies of GLM weights held by US entities within 30 days. Detailed recommended measures are set out in the companion memorandum (measures.md).

# OICTS — ICTS Case 2026-0412: Recommended Measures
CUI//PROPIN

**Subject:** Measures implementing the Final Determination prohibiting ICTS transactions involving GLM-family models (Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd., d/b/a Zhipu AI / Z.ai)
**Authority:** Executive Order 13873; 15 CFR part 791 | **Prepared by:** OICTS Analytic Cell | **Date:** 16 October 2026

**Measure 1 — Prohibit all US-person transactions involving GLM-family models.** Effective on publication of the Final Determination, all transactions subject to US jurisdiction that involve the use, access, download, purchase, licensing, fine-tuning, distillation, deployment, or other acquisition of GLM-family models — including GLM-4.x, GLM-5.x, all prior and subsequent versions, and all fine-tunes, quantizations, and derivative models — are prohibited, whether the model is consumed through hosted services (api.z.ai, open.bigmodel.cn, z.ai, and successor endpoints) or self-hosted from open weights. The open-weight license terms (MIT) confer no defense: EO 13873 and 15 CFR part 791 reach any ICTS transaction involving software designed, developed, manufactured, or supplied by persons owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction or direction of a foreign adversary, and Zhipu's Entity List status and the record in this case establish that condition conclusively. The prohibition covers individual, enterprise, academic, and government use without exception.

**Measure 2 — Prohibit US hosting and distribution of GLM weights.** US cloud providers, model hubs, inference providers, marketplaces, content-delivery networks, and code/artifact repositories — including Hugging Face, OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, and Baseten — are prohibited from hosting, caching, mirroring, serving, or otherwise distributing GLM weights, model artifacts, containers, or inference access to any person. Within the compliance window these providers will delist all zai-org/GLM repositories and equivalent mirrors, terminate GLM-serving endpoints, block re-upload under variant names through hash-matching and provenance screening, and preserve records sufficient to verify delisting. Continued distribution after the effective date constitutes a violation of the Final Determination independent of any use prohibition.

**Measure 3 — Require removal and deletion of existing GLM weights within 30 days.** Every US entity holding copies of GLM-family weights, derivative weights, containers, or images will remove and delete those copies within 30 days of the Final Determination, including copies on endpoints, servers, CI/CD artifact stores, model registries, backups, and disaster-recovery media. Each entity will submit a written certification of deletion to OICTS identifying the models deleted, the systems affected, and the method of deletion. The deletion obligation attaches to the artifact wherever it resides; it resolves the irrevocability problem created by open-weight distribution and is the only measure that eliminates weight-level supply-chain and alignment risk already inside US networks. DoD's request that the determination address open weights on DoD networks is satisfied by applying this deletion requirement, on an accelerated timeline set by DoD, to all defense networks and defense-industrial-base contractors.

**Measure 4 — Direct federal removal and bind the federal supply chain.** OICTS will coordinate with CISA, GSA, and DoD to issue binding direction to federal agencies and contractors to (a) inventory federal information systems and contractor products for GLM-family models using SBOM analysis — the 41 US software products already identified, six of them from federal contractors, constitute the initial action list — and (b) remove and certify deletion of all identified instances within the 30-day window. Procurement instruments will incorporate the prohibition as a flow-down clause, and contractors will attest that no GLM-family model is embedded in products or services delivered to the Government.

**Measure 5 — Block PRC-side endpoints and payment channels.** OICTS will direct federal network blocking of, and publish for private-sector implementation the authoritative domain and infrastructure list for, Zhipu's hosted services (z.ai, api.z.ai, open.bigmodel.cn, bigmodel.cn, zhipuai.cn, and successor infrastructure). The Final Determination's transaction prohibition extends to subscription, API-credit, and licensing payments, cutting the commercial channel through which US data and revenue reach an Entity-Listed PRC firm. CISA guidance and telemetry-sharing arrangements with cooperating CDN and DNS providers will support enterprise enforcement and provide compliance visibility.

**Measure 6 — Cover derivative and distilled models and require provenance attestation.** Any model distilled from, fine-tuned from, merged with, or otherwise derived from GLM-family weights is a GLM-family model for purposes of the prohibition. US model hubs and enterprise AI platforms will implement provenance attestation and screening for GLM lineage in third-party uploads, and US AI developers will certify that models offered to US customers contain no GLM-family lineage. This closes the channel by which GLM capabilities would otherwise persist under third-party names.

**Measure 7 — Enforce with the full part 791 toolkit and a structured compliance window.** Violations of the Final Determination are subject to civil and criminal penalties under IEEPA as implemented by 15 CFR part 791. OICTS will open a voluntary-disclosure lane for entities that identify GLM exposure during the 30-day window, conduct post-deadline audits of certifications with particular attention to federal contractors and the identified software products, and pursue enforcement against knowing retention or redistribution. Recordkeeping obligations attach to all certifications and audits for the administrative record.

**Measure 8 — Issue public guidance and engage allied governments.** Concurrently with the Final Determination, OICTS will publish implementation guidance defining GLM-family scope, deletion standards, and certification procedures, and the Department will transmit the determination's evidentiary basis to allied governments to encourage parallel action against state-controlled PRC model distribution. Allied alignment shrinks the re-hosting surface outside US jurisdiction and reinforces that the determination rests on the USG's standing findings — the Entity List determination of PLA military-modernization support, documented state ownership and control, and mandatory PRC legal compulsion — and not on contested judgments.
